features.name: Subtree export/import protocol
features.description: Moves authority over a dirfrag subtree (down to its nested bounds) from exporter rank to importer rank using the EXPORT_* (LOCKING, DISCOVERING, FREEZING, PREPPING, WARNING, EXPORTING, LOGGINGFINISH, NOTIFYING, CANCELLING, CANCELLED) and IMPORT_* (DISCOVERING, DISCOVERED, PREPPING, PREPPED, LOGGINGSTART, ACKING, FINISHING, ABORTING) state machines and 10 subtree-migration messages (MExportDirDiscover/Ack, Prep/Ack, Notify/Ack, MExportDir/Ack, Finish, Cancel; 0x449-0x460, 0x454/0x455 defined but unused) plus 3 single-inode cap messages (MExportCaps/Ack, MGatherCaps; 0x470-0x472).
features.notes: MDS-MDS messages and journal events are internal (no interop with C++ ranks needed); the client-visible parts are cap EXPORT/IMPORT, forced sessions, request forwarding and export_targets.

features.name: Export preconditions and refusals
features.description: export_dir refuses when the dir is export-pinned elsewhere (unless stopping and non-empty), rank not active/stopping, FS read-only, dest not active, cluster degraded, system inode (root, .ceph, lost+found, ~mdsN, strays), frozen/freezing, already exporting, inside a stray dir not owned by dest, quiesced, or under quarantine.
features.notes: Refusals are silent (log only); admin 'export dir' still returns 0.

features.name: Balancer-driven export queue and size throttle
features.description: export_dir_nicely appends to export_queue; maybe_do_queued_export starts exports while total_exporting_size < 2*mds_max_export_size and the remaining budget covers one max_export_size per export still in LOCKING; clear_export_queue bumps export_queue_gen.
features.notes: Direct export_dir callers (export pins, admin, empty-import return) bypass the budget.

features.name: Export splitting of large subtrees
features.description: maybe_split_export estimates subtree size (800 per dirfrag, name length, null +1, remote +10, inode +1000, +80 per cap) and splits exports larger than mds_max_export_size into child exports sharing an export_base_t; the original is requeued after children finish.
features.notes: Heuristic units, not bytes.

features.name: Subtree freeze and auth-pin drain
features.description: CDir::freeze_tree marks every nested non-subtree dirfrag with a shared freeze_tree_state so no new auth pins are allowed (ERR_EXPORTING_TREE) and waits until in-flight auth pins drain; the importer freezes its replica region at prep. All requests that auth-pin objects in the region, client cap messages/releases and max_size changes on frozen inodes are deferred to WAIT_UNFREEZE.
features.notes: Main client-visible cost of migration: requests on the subtree block for the whole protocol duration.

features.name: Freeze deadlock breaker
features.description: find_stale_export_freeze cancels DISCOVERING/FREEZING exports whose cumulative auth pin count did not change for mds_freeze_tree_timeout (30 s) when remote auth-pin waiters exist (num_remote_waiters via Locker::notify_freeze_waiter) or the parent dir is freezing.
features.notes: Runs from MDSRankDispatcher::tick while active.

features.name: Quiesce and quarantine interplay
features.description: Exports of quiesced or quarantined inodes are refused; an export that would block on the quiescelock aborts; quiesce_inode cancels exports in LOCKING/DISCOVERING/FREEZING; the importer NACKs discovers through quiesced ancestors (path_traverse MDS_TRAVERSE_IMPORT -> -EAGAIN).
features.notes: Quiesce is driven by the volumes/snapshot workflows.

features.name: Export targets publication (MDSMap export_targets)
features.description: The exporter records hits on destination ranks (hit_export_target, decaying counters with mds_bal_target_decay); MDSRank::update_targets sends MMDSLoadTargets to the monitor each tick; an export waits (up to 4 MDSMap epochs) until dest appears in its own export_targets. Clients pre-connect to export targets; kclient reconnects to targets in up:reconnect.
features.notes: Bystanders that ack notifies are also hit as export targets (Migrator.cc:2262-2266).

features.name: Client session flush barrier (FLUSHMSG)
features.description: After the freeze completes the exporter sends CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG(seq) to every open, connected client session with CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER that holds caps in the region and waits for CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG_ACK before shipping MExportDir. The FLUSHMSG seq is the session's current push_seq (Session::wait_for_flush); FLUSHMSG_ACK completes all flush waiters at or below it.
features.notes: Clients flush pending cap releases before acking.

features.name: Prep: spanning-tree replication and bound opening
features.description: MExportDirPrep carries a replica of the base dirfrag, the bound list, per-bound traces (dentry/inode/dirfrag replicas from the bound up to the base) and the bystander set; the importer replicates them, discovers missing bound dirfrags (open_remote_dirfrag), pins bounds (IMPORTBOUND, stickydirs), force-wrlocks filelock/nestlock of the base inode, sets auth (E,I) and freezes.

features.name: Bystander warning/notify protocol
features.description: Ranks replicating the base dirfrag are warned (MExportDirNotify old=(E,-2) new=(E,I)) before the data is sent and notified (old=(E,I) new=(I,-2)) after EExport; abort variants restore (E,-2). Bystanders adjust their subtree map and ack; acks are faked for failed bystanders.
features.notes: Exists only because of cross-rank replication and cache-expire routing.

features.name: Metadata transfer encoding (MExportDir)
features.description: Pre-order dirfrag records with CDir::encode_export (fnode, dirty_old_rstat, committed_version, state, rep info, popularity, replicas), dentries (CDentry::encode_export: first, state, versions, full lock, replicas) with 'N' null, 'l' remote, 'i' primary markers; primary inodes carry CInode::encode_export (base inode/xattrs/snap/old_inodes/dirfragtree, state, pop, replicas, bound dirfrag stats, all nine lock states + loner, fcntl/flock tables) and Capability::Export maps with mds_caps_wanted; plus client inst/metadata maps.
features.notes: Transfers POSIX-relevant state (fcntl/flock locks, xattrs, dirty metadata) that must survive an authority change.

features.name: Forced client session open on importer
features.description: The importer creates/opens sessions for every client holding exported caps without client participation (prepare/finish_force_open_sessions), filters blocklisted clients, journals them in EImportStart (cmapv), sends unsolicited CEPH_SESSION_OPEN (queued in preopen_out_queue until the client connects), protects them via importing_count, and closes never-client-opened ones on reversal.
features.notes: Client REQUEST_OPEN on such a session is answered with OPEN only with CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE. Cleanup on reversal (dec_importing + close_forced_opened_sessions) only covers sessions in import_state.session_map, which is filled in import_logged_start; a reversal from IMPORT_LOGGINGSTART leaves importing_count raised (code reading, see open_questions).

features.name: Client capability migration (CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT/IMPORT)
features.description: Exporter sends EXPORT (cap_id, old mseq, peer{importer cap_id, issue_seq, mseq=old+1, mds or -1}) to every cap holder and drops caps; importer merges exported caps and sends IMPORT (new cap_id, seq, mseq=old+1, inode fields, snap trace, peer{exporter cap_id, seq, old mseq, exporter rank, FLAG_AUTH}). Clients accept either order; stale-mseq client messages are dropped.
features.notes: Cap state (issued/wanted/dirty flushes, max_size) must be preserved across authority changes for POSIX consistency of cached data/metadata.

features.name: Migration journaling (EImportStart, EExport, EImportFinish)
features.description: Importer journals a full copy of the imported metadata plus forced sessions in EImportStart before acking; exporter journals EExport (base, bounds, target) after the ack; importer journals EImportFinish(success) at the end or EImportFinish(false) on reversal. ESubtreeMap records in-flight imports as ambiguous_subtrees.
features.notes: cephfs-journal-tool decodes these C++ formats; a new on-disk format is free.

features.name: Ambiguous import resolution
features.description: After a crash, an import with EImportStart but no EImportFinish is ambiguous; the exporter claims the subtree in resolve iff EExport did not reach its journal; survivors in IMPORT_ACKING finish or reverse on the exporter's resolve; recovering importers disambiguate after all resolves; subtree resolves are withheld while migrations are in flight.

features.name: Cancellation and reversal on failure
features.description: export_try_cancel unwinds per state (unfreeze, unpin bounds, abort-notify bystanders, MExportDirCancel); export_reverse restores the exporter after importer failure in EXPORTING; import_reverse restores the importer (auth back, caps removed, sessions closed, EImportFinish(false)); any rank failure cancels all exports still in LOCKING..PREPPING on every rank.
features.notes: Kill points mds_kill_export_at 1-13 / mds_kill_import_at 1-10 enumerate crash points.

features.name: Empty import return
features.description: An imported dirfrag that is empty and whose inode is non-auth, or an empty non-auth subtree found during trim, is exported back to the inode's authority.

features.name: Stopping rank exports all subtrees
features.description: When max_mds is reduced, the stopping rank (not rank 0) exports every auth subtree (except mdsdir, frozen, ambiguous, exporting, ephemerally pinned) to the inode authority or rank 0 via the export queue, ignoring export pins.
features.notes: Shrinking ranks depends on migration completing. shutdown_pass clears the export queue and calls MDBalancer::handle_export_pins before queueing (MDCache.cc:8084-8086).

features.name: Single-inode non-auth cap migration (MExportCaps/MGatherCaps)
features.description: A replica rank holding client caps (read-only opens served by replicas) sends them to the auth on stray unlink or on MGatherCaps (sent by the auth when broadcasting quota); the auth journals ESessions, merges caps, sends IMPORT with CEPH_CAP_FLAG_RELEASE, and asks the replica (MExportCapsAck) to send EXPORT to clients without a connection to the auth.
features.notes: Silently dropped if the inode cannot be auth-pinned (FIXME).

features.name: Rename single-inode migration helpers
features.description: Cross-rank rename of a primary dentry migrates the inode with encode_export_inode/finish_export_inode/decode_import_inode/finish_import_inode_caps and Locker::xlock_export/xlock_import; client caps move with FLAG_AUTH IMPORT/EXPORT.
features.notes: Details in rename.md.

features.name: Delayed cache expires during migration
features.description: Replicas send MCacheExpire to both ranks of an ambiguous auth pair; exporter/importer queue expires for regions in transition (delayed_expire) and process or discard them depending on the outcome; nonces (EXPORT_NONCE=1) make exactly one side honor them.

features.name: Request blocking and forwarding around migration
features.description: Requests waiting on a frozen region are retried after unfreeze; on the old auth they are bounced to the client with MClientRequestForward (client must resend to the new auth); requests that would forward wait for single auth while authority is ambiguous.
features.notes: Visible as latency, not errors.

features.name: Migration perf counters
features.description: mds.exported, mds.exported_inodes (counts dentries), mds.imported, mds.imported_inodes, mds.subtrees; read by the dashboard.

features.name: Admin commands: export dir, dump_export_states
features.description: 'export dir <path> <rank>' starts an export of the path's frag_t() dirfrag (returns -ENOENT/-EINVAL for bad input, 0 otherwise); 'dump_export_states' dumps every export with state, state_history, peer, waiting sets, approx_size, freeze_tree_time.
features.notes: Used by qa/tasks/cephfs/test_exports.py.

features.name: Popularity transfer
features.description: The exported subtree's pop_auth_subtree is subtracted from ancestors on the exporter and added on the importer; popularity counters travel in the dirfrag/inode encodings.

features.name: Fault injection and thrashing
features.description: mds_kill_export_at (1-13), mds_kill_import_at (1-10) assert at protocol steps; mds_thrash_exports exports random dirs; mds_inject_migrator_session_race delays MExportDir until a client connects.
features.notes: Kill points define the crash cases recovery must cover.

features.name: Writeable-range reconciliation on cap import
features.description: When the importer creates caps from an auth export, clients listed in the inode's client_ranges get STATE_CLIENTWRITEABLE on their cap; if any client in client_ranges has no imported cap (no exported cap, or its session was filtered as blocklisted), the inode is marked STATE_NEEDSRECOVER so file size/mtime recovery runs later. Capability::merge ORs the exported CLIENTWRITEABLE/NOINLINE/NOPOOLNS/NOQUOTA state bits into the importer's cap.
features.notes: Keeps file size correct when a writer's cap is lost during the authority change.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around every migration step
serialization_points.shared_state: entire rank cache, subtree map, sessions, caps
serialization_points.why_serialized: Migrator has no private locking; all handlers and contexts run under mds_lock

serialization_points.name: Whole-region encode in one handler
serialization_points.shared_state: all objects of the exported region
serialization_points.why_serialized: encode_export_dir walks the full region synchronously under mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: O(region size) stall of the whole rank, up to ~20K inodes per export

serialization_points.name: Whole-region decode and EImportStart metablob build
serialization_points.why_serialized: decode_import_dir and metablob construction in one dispatch

serialization_points.name: Exporter subtree freeze
serialization_points.why_serialized: consistent snapshot of metadata, locks and caps for transfer; no auth pins allowed from DISCOVERING until export_finish
serialization_points.notes: Spans several MDS round trips, a client round trip per cap holder and 2+ journal flushes

serialization_points.name: Importer replica-region freeze
serialization_points.why_serialized: prevent replication/expire churn and requests until the import is final

serialization_points.name: Freeze drain of in-flight requests
serialization_points.why_serialized: freeze completes only when every auth pin in the region is released, including requests waiting on journal or peers

serialization_points.name: Exporter waits for entire journal safe
serialization_points.why_serialized: flush out e.g. pending cap imports before shipping
serialization_points.notes: Only entries touching the region/caps matter

serialization_points.name: Synchronous EImportStart and EExport journal writes
serialization_points.why_serialized: durable hand-off ordering: importer copy safe before ack, EExport safe before notify/finish
serialization_points.notes: Copy of the full region into the importer journal is the expensive part

serialization_points.name: Client session flush round trip
serialization_points.shared_state: client sessions with caps in the region
serialization_points.why_serialized: ensure cap-instantiating messages reached clients before IMPORT can overtake them on another connection

serialization_points.name: Bystander warning/notify round trips
serialization_points.shared_state: replica subtree maps on other ranks
serialization_points.why_serialized: cache-expire routing and authority knowledge on replicating ranks
serialization_points.notes: Only needed because of cross-rank replication

serialization_points.name: Export-target mon round trip
serialization_points.why_serialized: clients must see the target in the MDSMap to pre-connect
serialization_points.notes: Cancelled after 4 MDSMap epochs without the entry

serialization_points.name: Base/bound dirfragtreelock and ancestor snaplock rdlocks
serialization_points.shared_state: lock states of base inode, bound inodes, ancestors
serialization_points.why_serialized: no refragmentation of base/bounds and stable snaprealms while shipping
serialization_points.notes: Blocks fragmentation of bounds and snapshot ops on ancestors

serialization_points.name: Forced wrlock of base inode filelock/nestlock on both sides
serialization_points.shared_state: scatterlock state of the export root's inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: prevent fragstat/rstat gathers being counted twice or not at all during the authority change
serialization_points.notes: Blocks gathers (e.g. stat of the directory requiring SYNC)

serialization_points.name: Client cap message deferral on frozen inodes
serialization_points.shared_state: Capability state of inodes in the region
serialization_points.notes: Deferred flushes are dropped after export; clients re-send to the importer

serialization_points.name: Subtree resolve withheld during migrations
serialization_points.why_serialized: subtree claims must not race with in-flight authority changes
serialization_points.notes: Couples recovery of one rank to migrations on others

serialization_points.name: Any rank failure cancels early exports everywhere
serialization_points.why_serialized: avoid auth-pin deadlock with recovering ranks

serialization_points.name: MExportCaps inode auth pin + ESessions
serialization_points.why_serialized: sessions durable before caps are imported

external_contract.detail: head.cap_id = exporter cap id, head.migrate_seq = old mseq, caps/seq zero; ceph_mds_cap_peer{cap_id, issue_seq, mseq=old+1, mds (or -1 to drop), flags=0} encoded in the body in place of size/max_size (ceph_mds_caps_export_body, zero padded). If the client holds no cap from the target it opens a target session and creates a placeholder cap (seq=issue_seq-1, mseq, exported issued bits); if it already holds a target cap with cap_id == peer.cap_id and an older seq, that cap absorbs the issued bits; in all cases the exporter's cap is removed without a release.

Full cap grant from the new auth (cap_id, seq, pending, wanted, mseq=old+1, realm, inode fields, snap trace) plus peer{exporter cap_id, exporter seq, old mseq, exporter rank, CEPH_CAP_FLAG_AUTH or CEPH_CAP_FLAG_RELEASE} appended after the flock blob (CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER). Auth switch requires mseq strictly newer; client removes the matching peer cap, kicks cap flushes and re-requests max_size.

Same semantics as kclient, but EXPORT keys on peer.cap_id (0 -> drop the cap, I_CAP_DROPPED if wanted/issued) and IMPORT only looks for the peer cap when peer.cap_id != 0; auth switch uses ceph_seq_cmp(auth_cap->mseq, mseq) < 0 (Client::add_update_cap); IMPORT kicks flushing caps and resets requested_max_size when it becomes auth.
NFS-Ganesha relies on libcephfs to follow EXPORT/IMPORT and request forwards; synchronous NFS ops see the freeze as latency.

Client cap updates and releases carry migrate_seq; the MDS drops those older than the current cap mseq and drops messages for inodes/caps no longer present after export; clients must re-send flushes after IMPORT.
MDS sends FLUSHMSG(seq) to sessions with CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER; client flushes cap releases and replies FLUSHMSG_ACK(seq); used as an ordering barrier before shipping caps.
Client sends pending cap release then FLUSHMSG_ACK with the same seq.

Importer opens sessions without a client request and sends OPEN (queued until the client connects); client REQUEST_OPEN on such a session (once OPEN, rank not stopping) gets another OPEN with the push seq only if the client has CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE; otherwise it is dropped.
Kernel client opens sessions to export targets of laggy ranks and reconnects to ranks in up:reconnect that are listed as export targets even without an existing session.
Client connects to export targets of a rank on session open, on active map updates and on reconnect.
{global_id, set<rank> targets}; mon stores in mds_info.export_targets; requires mds 'x' cap; exporter waits until the target appears.
Requests reaching the old auth (or retried after unfreeze) are bounced with client_must_resend=true to the new auth.
Both messages carry the MDS's current OSD epoch barrier.
u64 counters (exported_inodes/imported_inodes count dentries); dashboard reads them.
export dir returns {return_code}; dump_export_states returns per-export tid/path/dirfrag/state/state_history/peer and phase-specific fields.
C++ encodings (EExport v4, EImportStart v4, EImportFinish v3) decoded by cephfs-journal-tool; not binding for a new on-disk format.

rust_implications.topic: Intra-rank shard moves are invisible to clients
rust_implications.implication: If subvolume/subtree shards move between cores or worker groups inside one rank, no EXPORT/IMPORT, session or export_targets protocol is needed; only moves between ranks (different MDS daemons/addresses clients route to) must emit the C++-compatible client protocol.

rust_implications.topic: Inter-rank authority moves must speak the cap migration protocol
rust_implications.implication: Any change of authoritative rank for an inode with client caps must send CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT from the old rank and CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT from the new rank with the exact peer block layout (EXPORT: in place of size fields; IMPORT: after the flock blob), mseq incremented by one, issue_seq consistency (placeholder seq = issue_seq-1), and FLAG_AUTH/FLAG_RELEASE semantics; clients must be able to receive them in either order.

rust_implications.topic: mseq-based fencing of stale client messages
rust_implications.implication: The Rust cap table must keep a per-cap migrate_seq and drop client cap updates/releases with an older mseq after an authority change; clients rely on this and re-send flushes on IMPORT.

CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG/ACK is the only client-supported per-session ordering barrier; a Rust cross-rank move that ships cap state should use it (or prove cross-connection ordering otherwise) for clients with CEPH_FEATURE_EXPORT_PEER.

rust_implications.topic: Forced sessions on the target rank
rust_implications.implication: The target rank must be able to create and persist client sessions it never saw (from the source's inst/metadata), send unsolicited CEPH_SESSION_OPEN, queue messages until the client connects, protect them from autoclose/eviction while the move is in progress, and close them if the move aborts (otherwise clients get evicted after session_autoclose).

rust_implications.topic: MDSMap export_targets must still be maintained
rust_implications.implication: kclient reconnect logic and libcephfs pre-connection depend on export_targets; the Rust MDS should publish target ranks via MMDSLoadTargets before moving authority to them, and may keep it populated permanently for peer ranks of a sharded deployment.

rust_implications.topic: Avoid full-subtree freeze for the whole protocol
rust_implications.implication: C++ blocks every request on the subtree across several MDS round trips, a client round trip per cap holder, a rank-wide journal sync and a full-copy journal write. A Rust design with per-shard journals can hand over the shard's journal stream/objects by reference (on-disk format is free) and fence only the commit point, shrinking the blocked window to one fencing epoch.

rust_implications.topic: No re-journaling of the whole region
rust_implications.implication: EImportStart copies all imported metadata into the importer journal. With per-shard journals in RADOS shared by ranks, the importer can replay/adopt the shard journal instead; dirty state needs no copy.

rust_implications.topic: Replace ambiguous-import resolution with explicit 2PC records
rust_implications.implication: C++ resolves crashed migrations through resolve-stage subtree claims, holds back resolves during migrations and cancels early exports cluster-wide on any rank failure. A shard ownership record (e.g. versioned in RADOS or the mon) with 2PC prepare/commit gives a deterministic outcome without coupling all ranks' recovery.

rust_implications.topic: Bystander protocol only exists because of replication
rust_implications.implication: If the Rust MDS avoids cross-rank metadata replication (clients are forwarded instead), the warning/notify/expire-delay machinery is unnecessary; if replicas are kept, an equivalent invalidation protocol is needed.

rust_implications.topic: File locks and xattrs must move with authority
rust_implications.implication: fcntl/flock tables, xattrs, snaprealm data, client_ranges (writeable ranges, NEEDSRECOVER) and loner state are part of the transferred state; POSIX lock semantics must survive a shard move.

rust_implications.topic: Dentry leases on the old rank
rust_implications.implication: C++ leaves client dentry leases attached to the old rank's replica dentries and revokes them through replica lock messages. Without replicas, a Rust move must revoke leases (CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE) or keep the old rank answering lease traffic until they expire.

Requests reaching the old rank after a move must be bounced with MClientRequestForward (client_must_resend); completed-request tracking is per rank in C++, so a Rust design should migrate per-session completed request ids with the shard to keep replay safe.

Because a C++ migration blocks all requests on the subtree, a moving subvolume would violate its SLA; Rust shard moves should be throttled per shard and scheduled by the QoS layer, not by a rank-wide size budget.

MExportCaps/MGatherCaps exist because replicas can issue read caps; if only the authoritative shard issues caps, this mechanism disappears, but quota broadcasts still need every cap holder to be known to one owner.
Ganesha clients see freezes as latency spikes; any automatic rebalancing in Rust must be incremental or off the hot path for Ganesha-heavy subvolumes.

open_questions: Is the ceph_assert in Migrator::import_logged_start (Migrator.cc:3196-3197) reachable when the exporter fails while the importer is in IMPORT_LOGGINGSTART with no bystanders (import_reverse erases import_state before EImportStart becomes safe)? With bystanders, sessions prepared by prepare_force_open_sessions seem to stay OPENING with importing_count incremented. Not reproduced.
Is it intentional that handle_export_notify_ack hits the sender (a bystander) as an export target (Migrator.cc:2262-2266)?
mds_thrash_exports marks the export root instead of the randomly chosen child as STATE_AUXSUBTREE (Migrator.cc:976-986); test-only, probably a bug.

CDentry::finish_export does not twiddle the dentry lock state; this relies on frozen dentries being in states whose replica state equals the auth state (SYNC/LOCK). Confirm no other states are possible at export time.
import_state_t::updated_scatterlocks is filled but never consumed; confirm it is dead state.

The rationale for CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG before export (cross-connection ordering of cap-instantiating messages versus importer IMPORTs) is inferred from the code comment; confirm against upstream design history.

import_reverse drops PIN_IMPORTINGCAPS only in IMPORT_ACKING (Migrator.cc:3067-3088); the pins taken by decode_import_inode_caps during handle_export_dir are never released when the import is reversed from IMPORT_LOGGINGSTART, so those inodes can never be trimmed. Code reading only.

A session whose importing_count leaked after a LOGGINGSTART reversal may later trip ceph_assert(!session->is_importing()) in Server::close_forced_opened_sessions (Server.cc:1174) if another import that force-opened the same session is reversed from ACKING. Speculative, not reproduced.

Migrator::import_reverse's mds->is_resolve() branch (trim_non_auth_subtree) appears unreachable: import_reverse is called from handle_mds_failure_or_stop and from MDCache::handle_resolve only on surviving (clientreplay/active/stopping) ranks, and import_state is in-memory only.
